dimensions.note: key and password are sensitive; a PEM reaches cosign only as COSIGN_KEY in the subprocess environment, the passphrase as COSIGN_PASSWORD; argv shows <pem> in errors and the PEM is masked in everything cosign prints; the passphrase is not masked on purpose, cosign never prints it and a short one would mangle parsed output (found by the live test). generateKeyPair records the private key as a sensitive field. The keyless arguments, identity, regexp and issuer, are public by nature and recorded in the signer record.
Every method logs intent and outcome with structured placeholders; no secret is logged; the fingerprint, not the key, identifies the public key.

Tags, bad annotations, an empty key, an unreadable predicate or file are refused before cosign runs; a verification that fails is a record with cosign's reason, any other cosign failure throws before writing; JSON cosign prints is checked before use; a public key whose PEM body is not base64 is named as such; a CRLF PEM is accepted as cosign accepts it. Keyless: an identity without an issuer, an issuer without an identity, both identity forms, a public key beside an identity and tlog false with an identity are refused by the arguments check and again in verifyFlags before cosign runs; cosign's keyless verdict, none of the expected identities matched, is a record, not a failure.

32 unit tests with a fake cosign cover describe, generateKeyPair, sign, verify, attest, verifyAttestation, signBlob, verifyBlob, masking, CRLF PEMs, name uniqueness, the parsers, the checks, verifyMode, the keyless argv of verify, verifyAttestation and verifyBlob, and every keyless refusal; the COSIGN_E2E test ran cosign 3.1.4 against a throwaway registry: key pair, sign, verify, wrong key, attest, verify-attestation, blob signed, verified and tampered; the COSIGN_KEYLESS_E2E test verified cgr.dev/chainguard/static by digest against Chainguard's release workflow identity and GitHub's issuer through the public Sigstore instance, its SPDX attestation too, and saw another identity fail with none of the expected identities matched; the two workflows and @dataverket/ko-signed-images ran live with a vaulted key in the previous round and are unchanged.

sign, attest and signBlob are additive: a second run adds a signature or rewrites the bundle, nothing is lost; temporary files (signing config, public key, key pair, bundle paths) are removed in finally.
No HTTP of its own; the contract is cosign 3.1.4's CLI, whose JSON output and exit codes the tests pin.
Scratch removes every temporary file on every path; stdin is closed so cosign cannot prompt; subprocesses take the context signal.
README, skill and tests use registry.example.org, example PEMs and 127.0.0.1:5000 for the throwaway registry; no real infrastructure named.

Closed z.object schemas throughout; every hash field, the signer's fingerprint, a predicate's and a file's sha256, has the sha256: prefix; keypair.passphraseSet says whether a passphrase was given, since cosign's PEM is always an encrypted block; signer.verifyMode is an enum of key, keyless, none and the three identity fields are recorded as given.
Every resource spec declares lifetime infinite and garbageCollection 10.
A signature is not a managed resource: created and verified, never updated or deleted here.

arguments (policy), cosign-installed (local, live) and key-usable (live, before sign, attest and signBlob); arguments now also judges the keyless set as a whole; an auto-definition's vault text fails arguments by design, with a message saying to run the workflow.

signer, keypair, <spec>-<repository, sanitized>-<12 hex of digest> and <blob spec>-<file name>-<12 hex of the path's sha256> never collide across specs; one digest in two repositories, or two files of one name in two directories, give two records, as a test proves.
No method reads stored data back.
Unpublished, so the version stays 2026.10.28.1 and no upgrade entry is needed; the three keyless arguments default to empty, so an existing signer definition parses unchanged.
